channel.title: # 🇱🇰 This Week in Sri Lanka
channel.description: Generated by gpt-5 from 276 English News Articles published between 2026-07-03 and 2026-07-10.

item.title: Authorities launched multiple probes after the deadliest prison unrest in years.
item.description: Investigators from specialised crime units opened parallel inquiries, and a three‑member committee with a retired apex court judge began an independent review. Rights officials also announced they were examining allegations that transferred detainees suffered ill‑treatment and that monitors were briefly denied entry during night‑time checks. Officials confirmed that security equipment including a body scanner and surveillance cameras was smashed, and that selected prisoners were relocated to higher‑security facilities. Lawmakers cited chronic overcrowding and staffing gaps, and outlined plans to expand capacity by roughly 10,000 places and to draft a House Arrest Bill to enable electronic monitoring in suitable remand cases.

item.title: Officials reported a sharp rise in dengue cases and deaths nationwide.
item.description: Health data showed the tally had reached 65,034 infections and 45 fatalities by 9 July, with about 1,300 new patients logged in a single day. Major hospitals reported congestion, while district inspectors said even frontline staff had fallen ill and courts imposed Rs. 12.25 million in fines in June for breeding‑site violations. Policymakers said they were assessing an internationally used vaccine and the Wolbachia method (a biological control that uses bacteria inside mosquitoes to reduce virus transmission). Clinicians noted that a licensed shot demonstrated over 90% effectiveness against the prevailing type 2 strain in trials conducted in the country, and authorities signalled readiness to deploy targeted units and dedicated high‑dependency care.

item.title: Research houses forecast muted earnings in 2026 before a rebound next year.
item.description: Analysts maintained an 8.2% growth outlook for corporate profits this year after a 25.5% surge in 2025, citing high input costs, tariff revisions and currency volatility compressing margins. They projected a 14.0% recovery in 2027 on normalising energy prices and a possible 50‑basis‑point policy rate cut (a reduction of 0.50 percentage points in the benchmark interest rate). Quarterly results already showed a third straight decline, with the food, beverage and tobacco segment dragging the aggregate, while banks were seen as relatively resilient on repricing dynamics. Equities were expected to trade sideways within historical valuation bands through year‑end as fixed‑income yields compete for capital.

item.title: Lawmakers approved stronger anti‑money‑laundering enforcement at second reading.
item.description: The bill passed with 154 votes in favour and two against, and will require a special majority before enactment. Earlier deliberations highlighted plans to give the financial‑intelligence unit a clear legal footing and to place the national coordinating committee in statute with escalation powers to Cabinet. Finance overseers also queried long‑term independence for investigators housed within the central bank, even as officials argued that global standards accept administrative models if operational autonomy is preserved. The reform is part of a broader effort ahead of the next mutual evaluation by international standard‑setters.

item.title: Rights commissioners ordered full access to all detention facilities during the unrest fallout.
item.description: Directives instructed top prison officials to protect inmates from reprisals, preserve evidence and cooperate with ongoing investigations. The watchdog also flagged a reported custodial death at a major remand complex and announced a rapid‑response review.

item.title: Ministers outlined electronic monitoring for select remand cases to ease overcrowding.
item.description: A drafting committee was appointed to prepare a House Arrest Bill, while administrators acknowledged delays at the analyst’s department and bail pathways for minor possession cases as pressure points. Plans to add prison places and tackle staff shortages were tabled alongside the legislative track.

item.title: Officials moved to restore a key wildlife corridor in the North Central dry zone.
item.description: An inter‑agency meeting agreed to clear traditional routes linking forest blocks around Mahakanadarawa, Nachchaduwa and Mahawilachchiya, and to use GPS and satellite tracking to map movements. Initial steps toward declaring the link between two reservoirs a sanctuary were discussed to cut conflict and improve habitat connectivity.

item.title: Maritime forces intercepted a beach consignment of contraband consumer goods.
item.description: A joint team recovered 15 parcels on the northwestern coast containing about 143,600 pharmaceutical capsules, 22,064 shampoo packets and 3,816 mosquito‑repellent tubes. Police took custody of the seizure for legal action.

item.title: Supervision was extended on a primary‑dealer firm at the centre of past bond scandals.
item.description: Regulators renewed a six‑month suspension from 5 July to continue investigations under debt‑securities law. The order keeps the entity barred from primary‑market activity pending the outcome.

item.title: A planned mass service‑cut drive for arrears was called off by the water utility.
item.description: Notices covering central urban divisions for 13–19 July were withdrawn, and prior announcements declared invalid. The board apologised for inconvenience caused by the cancellation.
